rules.statement: Never accept or return a secret-derived natural key (such as a hashed token key) on an administrative API; address such resources by a separate server-generated opaque id instead.
rules.why: A token-derived key in URLs, logs or responses leaks a token identifier; an opaque id keeps the admin identity separate from the runtime secret.
rules.check: Look for admin endpoint routes, request parameters or response DTOs that include a hashed key, token handle or other secret-derived lookup value instead of an opaque resource id.

rules.statement: Administrative projections of persisted grants or tokens must expose only metadata (ids, type, tenant, client, subject, lifecycle timestamps) and never the serialized payload or key material.
rules.why: The payload holds claims, tokens and subject material, and an admin needs none of it to triage or revoke. Exposing only metadata grants the least privilege.
rules.check: Check grant/token management DTOs and mappings for payload JSON, raw or hashed keys, or token values being copied into the response.

rules.statement: Implement revocation of a grant or token through a DELETE endpoint as an idempotent soft-revoke: set a revoked timestamp, keep the row, and return 204 even when the item is already revoked.
rules.why: Revocation must leave an audit trail, and a soft-revoke makes DELETE idempotent and safe to retry. Physical purging is a separate retention job.
rules.check: Look for revoke/DELETE handlers that physically remove grant rows, overwrite an existing revoked timestamp, or return an error for an already-revoked grant.

rules.statement: Generate opaque resource ids (including ids for runtime-minted artifacts) with the shared CSPRNG-based resource-id generator, assign them at creation, and store them in a unique-indexed normalized column.
rules.why: Every resource id should use the same 128-bit CSPRNG/base64url scheme, and admin lookup by id needs a unique, normalized column.
rules.check: Look for new resource ids made with Guid.NewGuid, counters or custom randomness instead of the shared generator, or for id columns that lack a unique index on the normalized value.

rules.statement: Make tenant query filters on entities with an optional tenant null-safe, so that tenant-scoped requests see only rows from their own tenant and never rows that have no tenant.
rules.why: Grants may have no tenant. The null-safe filter means global rows are not loaded in tenant-scoped requests.
rules.check: Check global query filters on entities with a nullable tenant navigation or FK and confirm they guard against null (e.g. `Tenant != null && ...`) and do not match null-tenant rows.

rules.statement: When an entity has no non-secret natural key, order keyset pagination on its chronological surrogate id, never on a secret-derived key.
rules.why: Ordering or making cursors from a secret key would put that key in cursors. The surrogate id gives a stable order that leaks nothing.
rules.check: Look for paged queries or continuation cursors built from hashed keys or other secret columns.
